rule: Exact both ways: an unwaived tab-walk difference or finding fails under its WCAG clause, a waived one whose lines changed fails until it is re-measured, and a row with nothing left to waive fails until it is deleted. order rows hold the cross-lane order diff as T-943's position-anchored hunks, as laneHunks writes them ('@@ #k', then two lines of context and '- ' React-only and '+ ' Blazor-only walk lines), so a waived difference that moves fails as changed; they take no host. findings rows hold each lane's complete sorted finding lines, optionally for one host. budget rows give a scenario whose own key handling is too slow to walk in full a fixed number of presses per walk (presses) and the press cost its test allowance is sized for (pressMs); they take no host. A wall-clock deadline is never waived. Every row names the open ticket that owns the fix and a reason a reviewer can check.

divergences.reason: The Blazor scheduler is a different component (T-146). With 256 events it renders 264 tab stops where React renders 9, and its own focus handling costs about 380 ms a Tab press (the walk's keydown work is under 10 ms of that), so a full Blazor walk would take about 100 s in each direction. Each walk stops after 24 presses, which covers React's whole walk, and is recorded as that budget on every host; the test allowance is sized for 400 ms a press.
